friction_audit.method: acted as a first-time Linux user through the full A-K journey (Section 1 of the Phase 30 task): obtain package -> install -> --version -> --doctor -> --list-devices -> point at a local GGUF -> inspect compatibility -> inspect plan -> run inference -> understand a failure -> uninstall
found_and_fixed_this_phase: no lightweight way to check model compatibility before running it -- fixed with --inspect-model (reuses compat_check.c, no second implementation)
--doctor gave no next step -- fixed with a model/GPU-aware 'Next:' suggestion line
--doctor did not report model architecture or compatibility even when --model was given, despite the metadata read being cheap -- fixed (reuses the same GGUF-metadata-only read --inspect-model uses)
--doctor did not show the real detected CPU despite it already being in the same device enumeration it already fetched for the GPU count -- fixed (free, no new detection logic)

CPU and Vulkan CI packages shared the exact same filename (membrane_<version>_amd64.deb), a real collision risk for any future GitHub Release -- fixed with distinct package names (membrane vs membrane-cpu) and a documented official-package policy

--plan-only rejected the exact `--ctx N --auto --plan-only` invocation this project's own --help EXAMPLES text had shipped since Phase 13.2 (it requires --prompt, which plan-only never reads) -- fixed: an empty placeholder prompt is injected only when --ctx is explicit (so auto-sizing, the only real use of prompt content on this path, never applies) and only for --plan-only specifically
found_not_fixed_this_phase: membrane-run --help is long (~440 lines); QUICK START/EXAMPLES sections (Phase 28) already mitigate this for a first-time user, and shortening further risks losing genuinely load-bearing detail (KV precision/placement semantics) -- left as-is, matches Section 12's own 'deep docs stay deep' guidance
